Hi Lindsey / Marissa — thanks for the thread. A few details on our pen test and vulnerability management process that should help your vendor team evaluate risk: 

Pen test summary (attached): Redwood commissions annual third-party penetration tests and ad-hoc engagements for major releases. Our last external engagement was completed 2026-11-15; a redacted summary is attached (Redwood_PenTest-Summary-2026.pdf).

Vulnerability management & SLOs:
- Scanning cadence: weekly authenticated vulnerability scans across production stacks + continuous external scanning for public endpoints.
- Triage SLA: new findings triaged within 72 hours; severity classification (P0/P1/P2/P3) assigned at triage.
- Remediation target: P0/P1 issues targeted for mitigation or compensating controls within 30 days; P2 within 90 days, P3 per release cycle.
- Patch validation: regression tests and verification after fix; emergency hotfix pipeline for critical findings.

Disclosure and redaction policy:
- We can provide redacted penetration test reports that remove customer-specific test artifacts and sensitive exploit details.
- For findings that require non-disclosure for third-party vendor tools, we can provide a redaction confirmation letter signed by our security lead.
- If FinHealth requires an NDA or a secure upload portal (SFTP/secure Sharepoint/Docusign upload), we can accommodate that.

Evidence and timeline: once we receive your questionnaire, Stephanie will coordinate internal teams to return completed answers. For document-level evidence (SOC 2, policies), we typically deliver within 2-3 business days of request; for deeper artifact pulls we may need 5-7 business days.

Attachments: Redwood_PenTest-Summary-2026.pdf, Redwood_SOC2-Type2-2025.pdf

Let me know if you'd like a short call between FinHealth InfoSec and our security team to walk through the report.

—Rishi
